record.paper_title: Additive Combinatorics: A Menu of Research Problems
record.original_question: For a finite abelian group G, determine the maximum size of a subset A whose specified sumset operation avoids the identity element 0. This includes determining τ(G,h), τ(G,[1,t]), τ±(G,h), τ±(G,[1,t]), τ̂(G,h), τ̂(G,[1,t]), τ̂(G,N), τ̂±(G,h), τ̂±(G,[1,t]), and τ̂±(G,N), where the defining condition is that 0 is not contained in the corresponding unrestricted, signed, restricted, or restricted signed sumset.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group (written additively, with identity $0$) and let $A \subseteq G$ be a finite subset. For a positive integer $h$, define the following sumsets:

- Unrestricted $h$-fold sumset: $hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_i \in A\}$.
- Unrestricted signed $h$-fold sumset: $h_\pm A = \{\varepsilon_1 a_1 + \cdots + \varepsilon_h a_h : a_i \in A,\ \varepsilon_i \in \{+1,-1\}\}$.
- Restricted $h$-fold sumset: $\hat{h}A = \{a_{i_1} + \cdots + a_{i_h} : i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_h,\ a_{i_j} \in A\}$ (sums of $h$ distinct elements of $A$).
- Restricted signed $h$-fold sumset: $\hat{h}_\pm A = \{\varepsilon_1 a_{i_1} + \cdots + \varepsilon_h a_{i_h} : i_1 < \cdots < i_h,\ \varepsilon_j \in \{+1,-1\}\}$.

For a positive integer $t$ define $[1,t]A = \bigcup_{h=1}^{t} hA$, and analogously $[1,t]_\pm A$, $[1,t]\hat{}\,A$, $[1,t]\hat{}_\pm A$. Let $m = |A|$, and define $[1,m]\hat{}\,A = \bigcup_{h=1}^{m} \hat{h}A$ and $[1,m]\hat{}_\pm A = \bigcup_{h=1}^{m} \hat{h}_\pm A$.

A subset $A \subseteq G$ is called zero-sum-free with respect to a given sumset operation if $0$ does not lie in the corresponding sumset of $A$. Define the following maximum sizes of zero-sum-free subsets of $G$:

$$\tau(G,h) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin hA\},$$
$$\tau(G,[1,t]) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,t]A\},$$
$$\tau_\pm(G,h) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin h_\pm A\},$$
$$\tau_\pm(G,[1,t]) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,t]_\pm A\},$$
$$\hat\tau(G,h) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin \hat h A\},$$
$$\hat\tau(G,[1,t]) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,t]\hat{}\,A\},$$
$$\hat\tau(G,\mathbb{N}) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,|A|]\hat{}\,A\},$$
$$\hat\tau_\pm(G,h) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin \hat h_\pm A\},$$
$$\hat\tau_\pm(G,[1,t]) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,t]\hat{}_\pm A\},$$
$$\hat\tau_\pm(G,\mathbb{N}) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq G,\ 0 \notin [1,|A|]\hat{}_\pm A\}.$$

Determine each of these quantities as a function of the finite abelian group $G$ and the parameters $h$ or $t$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Davenport constant problem (closely related to $\hat\tau(G,\mathbb{N})$) is known only for special classes of finite abelian groups (e.g., $p$-groups and groups of rank at most 2); the general case remains open. The full family of $\tau$-type invariants for arbitrary finite abelian groups under all the listed sumset operations is widely regarded as open, with only partial results in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Davenport constant - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The exact value of D(G) is known for p-groups and for groups of rank at most two; for general finite abelian groups it is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The closely related Davenport constant is unknown for general finite abelian groups.
